items.title: Iranian football team member granted asylum changes mind, will return to Iran
items.description: Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke says one of the seven members of the Iranian women's football delegation granted asylum in Australia now wants to be returned to Iran.

items.title: Live: Iran vows retaliation for US-Israeli strikes on residential areas
items.description: A spokesman for the Iranian armed forces also accused the US and Israel of using civilians as human shields, an accusation often levelled by Israel at its enemies in the Middle East. Follow live.

items.title: Dubai's 'tranquillity shattered' as Iran makes UAE a primary target
items.description: The United Arab Emirates is reporting more Iranian attacks than any other country as Tehran continues to retaliate against US and Israeli strikes.

items.title: Hundreds of millions wagered on Iran through online betting markets
items.description: Gambling experts and US lawmakers have raised concerns about the ethics of online betting and whether insider information is being used to profit from war.

items.title: IDF build up on Israel-Lebanon border
items.description: An IDF military build-up on the Israel-Lebanon border is forcing hundreds of thousands of Lebanese people to seek refuge. Up and down the border there is the presence of Israeli tanks, soldiers and reservists. The UN says people displaced due to this military operation have limited options and it's causing a massive humanitarian crisis.  Let's take a closer look at what's unfolded.

items.title: Australia closes several Middle East diplomatic missions, Wong confirms — as it happened
items.description: Foreign Minister Penny Wong has confirmed Australia has closed several diplomatic missions in the Middle East amid the ongoing war.

items.title: New Nationals leader Canavan vows to 'fight back' for Australians
items.description: With a populist economic message, the new Nationals leader said local manufacturing and higher birth rates were key as he rejected the labels of "left" and "right" politics.

items.title: Commercial rat baits to be banned from supermarket shelves
items.description: Rat baits could soon be restricted to licensed operators, after a change in regulations from the Australian Pesticides and Vetinary Medicines Authority.

items.title: Government doubles graduate visa fee but some countries exempt
items.description: Tiered pricing for visas is being used to support Pacific nations but some fear it could be misused to target certain communities.

items.title: ASX posts modest win as Asian markets regain ground — as it happened
items.description: A positive day on the ASX 200 as Australia's market posts gains despite Westpac and the National Australia Bank predicting the RBA will lift rates by 25 basis points in March and May.

items.title: Man jailed for playing 'key role' in Sydney antisemitic attacks
items.description: Nicholas James Alexander was jailed for a maximum of five years for his role orchestrating a series of antisemitic attacks across Sydney, including the fire-bombing of a childcare centre.

items.title: Triple killer lived with two foster children, minister lashes department
items.description: NSW Minister for Families and Communities Kate Washington says the mistake is the worst she has seen in her time in the portfolio.

items.title: Live: Bundaberg flood extent may not be known for a week, but peak below expectations
items.description: Bundaberg is facing its worst flood in more than a decade, with the Burnett River peaking at about 7.4 metres. Follow live.

items.title: Tony Burke to speak to AFP about right-wing attack on Muslims
items.description: The home affairs minister says he will discuss an alleged right-wing attack on a Muslim community in regional Victoria with the federal police.

items.title: Katie Perry wins High Court trademark case against Katy Perry
items.description: Australian fashion designer Katie Perry wins her High Court battle against international pop star Katy Perry in a long-running trademark case.

items.title: WOMADelaide 2026 was pure joy — here’s what went down
items.description: At Adelaide's global music weekender, tens of thousands transform everyday anxieties into a shared burst of joy.

items.title: Main link between Sydney and western NSW to be closed for weeks
items.description: A crucial bridge on the Great Western Highway linking Sydney to the state's Central West will be shut for at least a fortnight, while specialists assess why it is moving and cracking.

items.title: Bus company linked to fatal wedding crash admits to heavy vehicle breaches
items.description: The bus company linked to the deadly 2023 Hunter Valley wedding bus crash and a director plead guilty to heavy-vehicle law safety breaches.

items.title: Man missing for months likely murdered in home, police say
items.description: Police believe a man who has been missing for more than four months in North Queensland was murdered in his home, and that his body was moved.

items.title: Ex-footballer Barry Cable abused young girls in backyard spas in Melbourne, court told
items.description: Former footballer Barry Cable sexually assaulted children in a backyard spa in Melbourne at a time when he was a "famous" figure, a court has heard.

items.title: Dispute over sacred site in central Queensland proceeds to civil trial
items.description: The dispute centres on the Doongmbulla Springs, near the Carmichael River in central Queensland, with traditional custodians accusing the Queensland government of failing to protect the sacred site.

items.title: Craig Freeman to stand trial over 1991 death of wife Melinda
items.description: Mr Freeman was charged last year for the murder of his then-wife, who was found dead in their home in Melbourne's north 30 years ago.

items.title: Police return to remote station in Gus Lamont search
items.description: SA Police have returned to the family's remote outback station as they continue their investigation into the disappearance of four-year-old Gus Lamont.

items.title: 'Bloody glorious' farewell for beloved drag star Maxi Shield
items.description: A pair of purple stilettos sat atop her white casket while family and friends shared their favourite memories of her.

items.title: NAPLAN resumes after technical issues paused online testing
items.description: NAPLAN testing for 1.3 million Australian school students resumes following technical problems that saw schools across the country unable to access the digital test.
